title: PP Dialect Completeness — Correction Factors, Rigid Tapping, Probing, Threading, Data Wiring
description: Close dialect gaps and wire remaining data files. Add Kienzle correction factors (K_gamma, K_kappa, K_wear, K_coolant, K_edge) into the force calculation path. Add rigid tapping (G84.2/G84.3), probing cycles (Renishaw/Siemens/Heidenhain), and threading cycles (G76/CYCLE206) to all 25 controller dialects. Wire AlarmRegistry, controller-alarm-database.json, fusion-post-strategies.json, and cimco-post-strategies.json into the pipeline.

engines: KienzleForceModelEngine — canonical Kienzle with correction factors
PostProcessorPipelineEngine — Stage 3.2 canned cycles, Stage 4.1 arc linearization

units.title: Add K_gamma, K_kappa, K_wear, K_coolant, K_edge correction factors to PP force calculation
steps: Read KienzleForceModelEngine to understand its correction factor implementation
In PostProcessorPipelineEngine Stage 1.1 (after base kc1_1 resolved from registry or canonical):
K_gamma = 1 - 0.01 * (gamma_rake_deg - 6) where gamma from ToolContext.rake_angle_deg
K_kappa = 1 - 0.015 * (kappa_deg - 45) where kappa from ToolContext.lead_angle_deg
K_wear = 1 + 0.5 * (VB_mm / 0.3) where VB from wear state (default 0 for fresh tool)
K_coolant = CoolantRegistry lookup (flood=1.0, MQL=0.95, dry=1.1, cryo=0.9)
K_edge = 1 + 0.002 * edge_radius_um (default 0 if unknown)
corrected_kc = kc1_1 * K_gamma * K_kappa * K_wear * K_coolant * K_edge
Add correction_factors object to stage output for auditability
Add constants to constants.ts if not already present
exit_conditions: Build passes, all tests pass
New test: 30° rake angle reduces kc by 24% (K_gamma = 0.76)
New test: MQL coolant reduces kc by 5%
New test: fresh tool (VB=0) has K_wear=1.0, worn tool (VB=0.3) has K_wear=1.5
Correction factors documented in analytics output

units.title: Add rigid tapping (G84.2/G84.3) and threading (G76/CYCLE206) to all 25 dialects
steps: Add to ControllerDialect interface: rigid_tap_cycle?: string, thread_single_point?: string, thread_multi_pass?: string
For each Fanuc dialect: rigid_tap_cycle = 'G84.2' (RH) / 'G84.3' (LH)
For Siemens dialects: rigid_tap_cycle = 'CYCLE84' with SPOS params
For Heidenhain: rigid_tap_cycle = 'CYCL DEF 207 (RIGID TAP)'
For Haas: rigid_tap_cycle = 'G84' with J (retract speed)
For Mazak: rigid_tap_cycle = 'G84' with Mazak rigid tap subprogram
For threading: Fanuc G76, Siemens CYCLE206/CYCLE207, Heidenhain CYCL DEF 262/263
For Swiss (Citizen/Star): add LFV chip breaking thread mode
Update translateCannedCycle() to handle rigid_tap and thread types
exit_conditions: Build passes, all tests pass
New test: Fanuc 31i dialect has rigid_tap_cycle = 'G84.2'
New test: Siemens 840D has thread_multi_pass = 'CYCLE206'
New test: translateCannedCycle('rigid_tap', 'fanuc_31i') returns G84.2

units.title: Add probing cycles to all 25 dialects
steps: Add to ControllerDialect interface: probing_cycles?: { auto_datum, surface_z, bore, boss, corner, tool_length }
Fanuc: G65 P9810 (Z surface), G65 P9811 (corner), G65 P9812 (bore/boss), G65 P9023 (tool length)
Siemens: CYCLE977 (datum), CYCLE978 (surface), CYCLE979 (bore/pocket)
Heidenhain: TCH PROBE 410-419 (datum/bore/boss/surface/corner/ridge)
Haas: G65 P9810-P9815 (Renishaw Haas variant with MFIN)
Add probing_cycles lookup to getFeatureCodes()
exit_conditions: Build passes, all tests pass
All 25 dialects have probing_cycles defined (or explicit 'none' for generics)
ProbingCycleEngine (from MS1) can use dialect probing_cycles for correct syntax

units.title: Wire fusion-post-strategies.json + cimco-post-strategies.json into Stage 3.2/4.1
steps: Read fusion-post-strategies.json — extract arc tolerance rules, linearization params, canned cycle mappings
Read cimco-post-strategies.json — extract drilling cycle mappings, helix linearization formula
Create CAMPostStrategyLookup: given controller family, return CAM-proven rules for arc handling, tolerance, cycle translation
In Stage 3.2 (motion dynamics): use CAM-proven arc max angle per controller instead of hardcoded 180°
In Stage 4.1 (if arc linearization exists): use CAM-proven segment_count formula
Log strategy source in analytics: 'fusion-post-strategies' or 'cimco-post-strategies'
exit_conditions: Build passes, all tests pass
New test: Haas controller uses 355° max arc (from Fusion strategy)
New test: Siemens uses 90° max arc (from Fusion strategy)
CAM strategy source appears in analytics

units.title: Wire AlarmRegistry + controller-alarm-database.json for alarm-preventive output
steps: Import AlarmRegistry (lazy load)
In Stage 5.1 (G-code safety analysis), after syntax check, query alarm database:
For each controller-specific M-code or G-code combination, check if known alarm conditions exist
Flag blocks that would trigger known alarms: 'Warning: This feed rate on Fanuc 0i-MF triggers alarm 414'
Add alarm_warnings[] to pipeline result
Add alarm prevention to Stage 6.8 (output verification): block output if critical alarms detected
exit_conditions: Build passes, all tests pass
New test: known alarm-triggering G-code combo produces warning
New test: unknown controller gracefully skips alarm check
Alarm warnings appear in analytics output
